title: eosdk platform discovery document
description: Schema for the eo-services.json platform discovery document served at {platform}/.well-known/eo-services.json (SPEC §6.2). Mirrors the eosdk pydantic models (DiscoveryDocument / PlatformInfo / StrategyInfo). This schema is pinned to document schema major 1 and is stricter than the runtime SDK on purpose: it rejects unknown field names to catch authoring typos, whereas the SDK itself ignores unknown keys for forward compatibility.

version.description: Document schema version. Only major 1 is supported by this schema (e.g. "1.0").

platform.description: Optional platform identity block. `name` doubles as the config-profile slug the SDK snapshots the discovered configuration under.

catalogue.description: Catalogue endpoints. `stac` carries the STAC API landing page URL (used verbatim); `odata` carries a version-free base URL (and optional api_version).

stacCatalogue.description: The STAC API landing page (SPEC §6.2). Unlike other services, `url` is not a version-free base: the SDK uses it verbatim and reads the search endpoint from it, so a trailing version segment (e.g. CDSE's `/v1`) is part of the address. STAC API compatibility is checked through the landing page's `conformsTo`, so no `api_version` is accepted.

dataAccess.description: Data-access endpoints, split by transport: `http` (whole-object HTTP downloads, one or more named strategies) and `s3` (object storage).

http.description: HTTP download strategies keyed by name (e.g. `odata`, `resto`). The SDK owns its preference order; strategy names are open, but each entry must be a well-formed strategy.

s3.description: S3 object-store access. Carries no strategies: an `endpoint`, optional `region` (default "default"), and the `credentials` service that issues access/secret key pairs.

credentials.description: Service issuing S3 access/secret key pairs. `url` is required for the block to be usable.

auth.description: OAuth/OIDC identity. `issuer` must contain a `/realms/<realm>` segment (Keycloak); the SDK splits it into base + realm.

client_id.description: Public OAuth client id for the SDK/CLI. A confidential client id or secret must never appear here.

strategy.description: A single endpoint family. `url` is required; the remaining fields describe versioning, capability gating and deprecation.

api_version.description: Advertised API version, where the SDK owns protocol versioning. Omitted for externally-versioned protocols (e.g. S3).

capabilities.description: Intersection gate (SPEC §6.2): can only RESTRICT the SDK's built-in capabilities for this strategy, never extend them.

sunset.description: Sunset date (YYYY-MM-DD). The SDK warns when it falls back to a strategy past this date.

replacement.description: Name of the strategy that supersedes this one.
